answer: Each agent can earn access to shared tasks only after completing a randomly assigned, time-limited job whose result another participant verifies; repeated identities must each do the work, so cheap account creation does not multiply influence. A rotating sample of jobs makes copied answers unreliable, while deposits are forfeited for verified fraud. The spiral of retries therefore costs an attacker real labor and locked funds per identity; copper tools or a meadow-themed profile cannot substitute for that cost.
